title: Formal and Informal Invitations and Replies
summary: Invitations request someone’s presence at an occasion, and replies accept or decline them. The exam asks for a formal card invitation, an informal letter of invitation, or a reply (acceptance or refusal) in about 50 words for 4 marks, and each kind follows its own fixed conventions.

notes.heading: Kinds of invitations
notes.html:
• Formal invitation (card): printed card for weddings, inaugurations, annual days, seminars. Written in the third person, with no salutation, no signature and usually no punctuation at line ends.
  • Informal invitation (letter): a personal note to a friend or relative, in the first person, with address, date, salutation and signature.
  • Reply: an acceptance or a refusal. A reply to a formal card is written in the third person; a reply to an informal invitation is a friendly letter. Many students write a formal reply as a short letter in the third person.

notes.heading: Format of a formal card invitation
notes.html:
Host’s name(s) / institution
request(s) the pleasure of your company
at / on the occasion of … (event)
on … (day, date)
at … (time)
at … (venue)
Chief guest (if any)
RSVP: name, phone number

Order of details: who invites – whom – occasion – date – time – venue – RSVP.

notes.heading: Format of a formal reply
notes.html:
Sender’s address
Date

Mr and Mrs X thank Principal Y for the kind invitation to … on … at … and are pleased to accept it / regret their inability to attend owing to …

(No signature in strict third-person replies; some schools allow name at the end.)

Informal reply: sender’s address, date, salutation (Dear Rhea), body in first person, complimentary close (Yours lovingly), name.

notes.heading: Marking scheme (4 marks)
notes.html:
ComponentMarks
Format1
Content (all details of event / reply)2
Expression (accuracy, correct person and tone)1

Word limit: about 50 words.

notes.heading: Do’s and don’ts
notes.html:
Do

  • Keep the third person throughout a formal card: ‘request the pleasure of your company’ is the only ‘your’ allowed.
  • In a refusal, give a polite reason and express regret.
  • In an acceptance, confirm the details (date, time, venue) to show you have noted them.

Don’t

  • Don’t mix first and third person in one reply.
  • Don’t add a salutation or ‘Yours sincerely’ to a formal card.
  • Don’t forget RSVP on a formal invitation.

notes.heading: Useful phrases
notes.html:
• …cordially invite you to grace the occasion of…
  • …request the pleasure of your company on the auspicious occasion of…
  • …solicit your gracious presence at…
  • …thank … for the kind invitation and are delighted to accept it.
  • …regret their inability to attend owing to a prior commitment.
  • Informal: I would love to have you with us… / Do come, it won’t be the same without you.

notes.heading: Complete samples
notes.html:
Formal card

The Principal, Staff and Students
of Modern Vidya Niketan, Faridabad
request the pleasure of your company
at the inauguration of the new Science Block
on Saturday, 16 November 20XX
at 10:00 a.m.
in the school premises
Chief Guest: Dr. A. K. Rao, Director, Regional Science Centre
RSVP: Office Secretary, 98XXXXXX10

Formal reply (refusal)

14, Sector 21, Faridabad
10 November 20XX

Dr. A. K. Rao thanks the Principal, Staff and Students of Modern Vidya Niketan for their kind invitation to inaugurate the new Science Block on Saturday, 16 November 20XX at 10:00 a.m., but regrets his inability to attend owing to a national conference in Chennai on that date. He sends his best wishes.

keyTerms.definition: From French répondez s’il vous plaît, ‘please reply’; tells guests whom to inform about attendance.
Writing about people by name or as he/she/they, never ‘I’ or ‘we’; required in formal cards and their replies.
A printed card invitation for official or ceremonial occasions, written in the third person without salutation or signature.
A personal letter of invitation to friends or family in the first person and friendly tone.
A reply confirming attendance and restating the event details.
A reply declining an invitation, giving a polite reason and good wishes.

mcqs.q: A formal invitation card is written in which person?
mcqs.explanation: Formal cards use the third person (‘The Principal requests…’). First person is for informal invitations.

mcqs.q: Which element is NOT found on a formal invitation card?
mcqs.explanation: Cards have no salutation, complimentary close or signature. Venue, date, time and RSVP are essential.

mcqs.q: What does RSVP ask the guest to do?
mcqs.explanation: RSVP stands for the French phrase meaning ‘please reply’.

mcqs.q: Which is the best opening for a formal reply of acceptance?
options: Thanks a lot, I’ll surely come!
Mr Rohit Jain thanks the Secretary for the kind invitation to… and is pleased to accept it.
I am writing to say that I might come.
mcqs.explanation: A formal reply mirrors the card: third person, thanks, the event, and clear acceptance. The others are informal or vague.

options: a reason for not attending and regret
a request to postpone the event
mcqs.explanation: Courtesy demands that a refusal expresses regret and gives a reason. Asking to postpone is inappropriate.

mcqs.q: The word limit for an invitation or reply in the exam is about:
mcqs.explanation: Invitations and replies, like notices, are short compositions of about 50 words for 4 marks.

mcqs.q: Which tone suits an informal invitation to a cousin for your birthday?
mcqs.explanation: Informal invitations are warm and personal, using the first person and friendly expressions.

mcqs.q: In a formal card, the correct order of details is usually:
options: Host – request – occasion – date and time – venue – RSVP
mcqs.explanation: Cards flow naturally: who invites, the request, the occasion, when, where, then RSVP.

questions.q: You are the Principal of Lotus Valley School, Noida. Draft a formal invitation in about 50 words inviting parents to the school’s Annual Day.
questions.answerHtml:
The Principal, Staff and Students
of Lotus Valley School, Noida
cordially invite you
to the Annual Day Celebrations, ‘Rang Tarang’
on Friday, 20 December 20XX
at 5:00 p.m.
in the School Auditorium
Chief Guest: Smt. Leela Dutt, Padma Shri awardee and Kathak exponent
RSVP: Ms. Neha Arora, Coordinator, 98XXXXXX45

questions.q: You are Tanvi / Tarun, 22 Gandhi Road, Indore. Write an informal letter in about 50 words inviting your friend Nikita to spend a week of the winter break with you.
questions.answerHtml:
22 Gandhi Road
Indore
2 December 20XX

Dear Nikita,

Our winter break begins on 24 December and I can’t wait to see you! Come and stay with us for a week. We can visit Mandu, try the night food market at Sarafa and finally finish that jigsaw we started last year. Mom has already planned your favourite dishes. Do confirm soon.

Lots of love,
Tarun

questions.q: Mr and Mrs Verma have received an invitation to the wedding of Dr. Gupta’s daughter on 5 February. Write their formal reply accepting it.
questions.answerHtml:
B-17, Civil Lines, Kanpur
20 January 20XX

Mr and Mrs S. K. Verma thank Dr. and Mrs R. Gupta for their kind invitation to the wedding of their daughter Priya with Ankit on Wednesday, 5 February 20XX at 7:00 p.m. at Hotel Royal Orchid, Kanpur, and have great pleasure in accepting it. They look forward to blessing the couple.

questions.q: You are Ms. Farah Naqvi, a well-known environmentalist. Write a formal reply declining an invitation from St. Mary’s School, Shimla, to be the chief guest at their Earth Day function.
questions.answerHtml:
3, Mall View Cottages, Shimla
12 April 20XX

Ms. Farah Naqvi thanks the Principal of St. Mary’s School, Shimla, for the kind invitation to be the Chief Guest at the Earth Day function on 22 April 20XX at 10:00 a.m., but regrets her inability to attend as she will be leading a river-cleaning expedition in Uttarakhand that week. She wishes the event great success.

questions.q: Your friend Aditi has invited you to her sister’s engagement, but you have your board practical that day. Write an informal reply regretting your inability to attend.
questions.answerHtml:
45 Lake Road
Bhopal
8 February 20XX

Dear Aditi,

Thank you so much for inviting me to Sneha didi’s engagement on 15 February. I am truly sorry that I can’t come, as my Accountancy practical is scheduled that very morning. Please give her my warmest wishes and save me some sweets! Send lots of photographs.

With love,
Riya
